transcript:
Header: 2025-12-31 09:00 UTC / Duration: 45m / Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (FinSight CTO), Ravi Patel (FinSight ML Eng), Sofia Gomez (FinSight VP Product)

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. um quick agenda - benchmark review vs the baseline provider, dig into a couple of outliers, and then next steps. maya, do you want to start with the numbers?

[00:18] Maya: yeah sure, i'll share my screen - i'm pulling up the spreadsheet we exported last night. so high level: our P95 for the redwood-hosted config with dedicated pool + prefix cache is 210ms for the 2k token sim prompts, and throughput sustained at ~120 rps per node with the batching config we used.

[00:38] Ravi: sorry can you repeat that, 210 p95 for which model and quant?

[00:42] Maya: yeah - this was with redwood-llama-13b q4f16 (quantized) on a single A10x node in the dedicated pool, with continuous batching window at 40ms and a small KV (k v) prefix cache enabled.

[01:05] Laura: baseline numbers from CloudModelCo show their P95 at 280ms on similar prompts but they report higher single-request latency variance. throughput plateaued around 80 rps.

[01:22] Ethan: so net-net we're seeing ~25% better P95 and ~50% higher sustained throughput on the same prompt set, correct?

[01:28] Maya: roughly yes, though there are a couple caveats - their infra used a different batch policy (larger window) so tail latency behaved differently; also their model was full-fp16 (not q4), which raises cost but can reduce some artifacts.

[01:48] Sofia: interesting - what about cold-starts and cache warmup? our production is very bursty first-12-hours each day.

[01:55] Maya: good question. we saw cold-start P95 of ~600ms on the redwood side for cold sessions before the kv prefix warmed. after 2k requests the cache hit rate stabilized and P95 dropped into the 200ms band. CloudModelCo reported similar cold starts but they had a higher baseline due to model spin-up times.

[02:20] Ravi: any concerns about output quality differences with q4f16 quant? we found a couple hallucinations in initial evals.

[02:27] Maya: we ran evals on the same prompt suite - quality delta was within your accepted threshold (we used your eval pass/fail criteria shared in week 1). there were a few edge cases, we noted them in the sheet (row 124-133). quantization introduced slightly shorter answers in some cases, but overall rouge/bleu metrics were comparable.

[02:55] Ethan: okay, let's talk about saturation testing - we ran sustained load for 10 minutes to simulate production bursts. maya, can you call out the throughput vs latency curve?

[03:04] Maya: sure - at low qps (10-50) p95 is stable ~180-220ms. as we move toward 120-140 rps per node, p95 climbs to ~320-380ms. beyond 160 rps we see queueing and latency spikes; CPU on the host stays low but GPU utilization hits 88-95% depending on sequence length.

[03:32] Laura: how does that compare to their baseline on the same hardware?

[03:36] Maya: CloudModelCo plateaued earlier - they saw saturation around 80-90 rps with P95 moving above 400ms at that point. their variance was lower under light load but got worse under heavy bursts.

[03:54] Ravi: you mentioned KV cache sizing. what hit rate did you see with our prompt patterns?

[03:59] Maya: for the prefix-heavy prompts (about 40% prefix reuse) we saw 65-72% hit rate with our 50k token KV window. for more unique prompts the hit rate drops to ~22%, so benefits are workload dependent. we included a recommended KV sizing chart in the sheet.

[04:20] Ethan: there were a few outlier tests where latency spiked unexpectedly. maya, any theory?

[04:25] Maya: yes - two main suspects: 1) occasional network jitter in the test harness (we saw packet retransmits around 12:14 UTC in the logs), and 2) garbage collection / scheduling on the host when other system processes kicked in during the longer sequences. we added annotations on the spreadsheet.

[04:44] Sofia: is the network jitter likely in our on-prem sim or Redwood infra?

[04:48] Maya: it looks like from the traceroutes it originated in your test sim environment (the traffic generator VM) - but we can re-run tests with a separate harness to be sure.

[05:00] Ethan: let's also talk cost - Ravi, you asked for cost per 1M tokens vs baseline. maya, you had a calc?

[05:07] Maya: yep - using our pricing model for the committed dedicated pool and assuming 70% KV hit, our estimated unit cost comes to about $45 per 1M tokens for the config we tested. CloudModelCo, per their publicly shared estimate and our test numbers, was ~ $62 per 1M tokens for similar throughput and quality. we put the detailed calc in the sheet (tab 'cost-comparison').

[05:28] Laura: so that's ~30% cheaper at similar or better latency - that's compelling. any enterprise drawbacks we should know? data residency / logs?

[05:36] Ethan: good point - for the private deployment we can offer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, and we have SOC2 attestation. maya, can you confirm log retention controls?

[05:46] Maya: yes - you can choose retention policies per route; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3/GCS with encryption. i'll link the SOC2 summary and retention options in the follow-up.

[06:00] Ravi: on networking we need to validate egress patterns for our regulated customers - we require no third-country egress for EU traffic. how do we handle region pinning?

[06:09] Maya: we support region pinning and can restrict routing to EU regions for those routes. for Private (VPC) deploys, traffic never leaves your VPC unless you configure egress. we'll cover the network diagram in the infra deep-dive.

[06:22] Laura: okay great. i want to ask about reliability: do you support automatic fallback to a smaller model during overload?

[06:28] Ethan: yes we have smart routing rules - you can configure cost-tier fallback (e.g., route to a 7b quant variant if 13b is overloaded) and automatic region fallback. we can demo the rollouts if you'd like.

[06:40] Sofia: one more question on benchmarking methodology - are the prompt sets identical and are you including client-side latency in the P95?

[06:47] Maya: methodology note: we used your shared prompt set (the 2500 prompts you provided) and ran both providers with the same harness; our P95 includes server-side processing plus network between harness and endpoint (so it's close to end-to-end). we call out client-side latency separately in the sheet.

[07:05] Ravi: earlier you mentioned variance - any idea why CloudModelCo has lower variance at low load but worse at high load?

[07:12] Maya: likely due to their batching window and scheduler - they batch aggressively at low QPS which smooths out variability, but their scheduler seems to have higher queueing delay under burst, causing longer tails. our continuous batching with short window trades a slightly higher baseline for better saturation behavior.

[07:35] Ethan: okay - moving into tuning recommendations. maya, top three knobs to hit both latency and cost targets?

[07:40] Maya: 1) batch window tuning - for your 95th P95 target we recommend 30-40ms window; 2) adaptive KV cache sizing based on observed prefix reuse - start with 50k token window and adjust after 1 week of production traffic; 3) quantization profile - q4f16 for latency-focused, consider q8 for some batch-heavy throughput workloads if you need lower cost but verify quality.

[08:04] Laura: if we need to run on-prem later, will the same configs transfer?

[08:08] Maya: yes the runtime and kernel selection is portable; the main differences will be network topology and available GPU types which will change the cost curve. we'll help produce a migration playbook.

[08:18] Ethan: quick note on security review - we heard earlier you need SOC2 docs and an encryption Q&A. i'll attach those.

[08:25] Sofia: thanks. can we get an estimate for a pilot dedicated pool cost for 3 months so finance can approve?

[08:30] Ethan: yes - i'll include a 3-month committed estimate in the follow-up with the cost breakouts we discussed.

[08:37] Maya: back to the benchmarks - we also ran a run with more aggressive batching (window 120ms) and full-fp16. in that run peak throughput hit 210 rps but P95 climbed to ~420ms; so if you prioritize throughput over latency you can push past 200 rps but tail suffers.

[08:58] Ravi: do you have any logs of per-token GPU occupancy? that might help us tune sequence-length throttles.

[09:03] Maya: yes - we exported the perf traces; i'll attach the perf traces tar in the follow-up. they include per-token GPU occupancy and kernel timelines.

[09:12] Laura: about the few hallucination cases you mentioned - are they more common with quant? any plan to mitigate?

[09:18] Maya: most are edge prompts where tokenization differences changed completion length; mitigations: small prompt engineering changes, temperature tuning, or keeping fp16 for the small subset of routes where you require max fidelity. we flagged the affected prompts in the sheet for review.

[09:35] Ethan: sounds good. let's surface immediate risks - any blockers from Redwood side to continue pilot?

[09:40] Maya: none. we need your infra folks for the deep-dive and the SOC2 contacts for compliance artifact exchange. also if you want lower cold-starts we can enable warm pools at some cost.

[09:52] Sofia: for the client team, next week we'll confirm who owns the infra deep-dive and provide our SIEM contact.

[09:58] Ethan: perfect. recap of next steps: share spreadsheet with annotated runs and cost calc; schedule infra deep-dive; customer to confirm stakeholders; and we'll re-run targeted benchmarks if you want a different batch/quant config.

[10:15] Laura: thanks everyone, that's helpful. appreciate the transparency on the numbers.

[10:20] Ethan: thanks all - we'll follow up with the sheet and deck by monday.

[10:25] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("K V" vs "KV" cache, "q4f16" sometimes transcribed as "q four f sixteen"), timestamps approximate.
